briefHtml:
Portfolio Brief — Mon 2026-10-12 (SGT)

  • SNAPSHOT BROKEN TODAY: navSgd prints S$21,340,507 — a +107% FX-outage artifact, not real. The watcher’s USD fetch timed out; fx table collapsed to SGD-only; foreign positions misconverted; riskFlags empty for the same reason. Last authoritative NAV: S$10,292,418 (Fri Oct 9, restated up +S$28,370 — restatement night 12).
  • Biggest mover (Fri): Xiaomi +9.72% to HK$25.96 — best day since July 8 — on SkyNomad pre-orders topping 70k in 30 days. Metals reclaimed: silver ~$60.4 +2%, GDX +2.95%. HSI +1.79% to 24,211; STI −0.20% (week −4.4%).
  • One thing: Trump’s Russian diesel deal (4M+ tonnes; US waiving energy sanctions through April) collided with the worst Gulf weekend of the war — 12 killed, 300+ injured at Riyadh airport, a third tanker mined in Hormuz, Trump mulling joining Saudi strikes on Houthis. Brent settled $104.72. Senators (Tillis) say the deal may be illegal.

State

  • Do not act on today’s snapshot: NAV/navChgPct/listedChgPct/riskFlags all unusable. priceErrors: L46.SI 404 (22nd session) + USD timeout.
  • FX (external): USDSGD ≈1.2810 steady, USDCNY ≈6.69 (yuan firmer), USDHKD 7.8473.

Friday closes

  • SGX: STI 5,401.89 −0.20%, 3rd straight decline, lowest since July 8; week −4.4%. DBS 73.36 −0.66%. YZJ led STI gainers.
  • HK buy-the-dip: HSI +1.79% to 24,211.35. Xiaomi 25.96 +9.72%. Tencent +3.3% ≈425 (back at trigger). SMIC +1.5% ≈57.65. Southbound volumes: Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC = 1/2/3.
  • US: SPX 7,811.54 +0.59%, Dow +0.83%, Nasdaq +0.64%; week SPX +1.2%. VIX 14.84 −3.7%. 10y 5.24% (+2bp; 52-wk high 5.311 Oct 5). Tech rebounded as Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects ≥$70bn annualized revenue by year-end. SpaceX spectrum deal: TMUS −13.3%, VZ −8.6%; towers +7–16%.
  • Metals: silver ~$60.4 +2% (zone held), gold ~$4,183 (GLD +1.57%), GDX 89.28 +2.95%, SLV +2.49%. Brent settled $104.72.

Insider / Congress

  • Wing Tai: Oct 6 filings (Change in Interests of Director + Grant of Share Awards) remain latest; none found for other held names. sginvestors
  • Congress: no new filings Oct 8–12. In window (Oct 7–12): PA Senate Dem 2x Dell Intl/EMC 5.6% 2033 bond buys, $1–15K each, filed Oct 7. Oct 5–6 items aged out. Unusual Whales

Policy watch

  • Russia diesel deal: 4M+ tonnes to US/global markets; sanctions waived through April; Zelensky team cut short US trip; Trump demands halt to refinery strikes, threatened intel/arms cutoff; senators demand reversal. Newsquawk
  • Gulf escalation: 12 killed/300+ injured at Riyadh airport Sat; Dammam hit Sun; 3rd tanker mined in Hormuz; US disabled blockade-breaching vessel; Iran’s Rezai threatened undersea cables/data centres/AI sites worth over $2tn; US accepted some of Tehran’s 7 conditions — Iran says insufficient.
  • EU-China: 16-point consensus; EU caps Chinese hybrid imports at 350k units yr 1, +6%/yr, 4 years — rare-earth threat moved to a negotiated track.
  • AI: NVDA in talks to raise/acquire Reflection AI (FT); AMZN discussing ~$7bn Decart deal (WSJ); OpenAI ≥$70bn by year-end (Bloomberg); US pushes AI-safety liability.
  • Energy plumbing: SPR emergency exchange up to 4M bbl (Isaias); IEA urged faster diesel releases; Trump told refiners to cut prices; oil execs withdrew from Riyadh congress.
  • China macro: Sep auto sales −24% Y/Y, NEV −12%; NDRC vows countercyclical support. SG Q3 GDP + MAS decision this week. Japan/Canada closed today.

Risk

  • Data risk is today’s headline: watcher FX layer failed — if USD feed stays broken at the 12:47 run, flags stay blind. Actual state = Friday’s restated S$10,292,418.
  • Policy-vs-physics divergence: pre-midterm fuel relief (diesel deal, SPR, IEA) vs worsening Gulf war; if Brent ~$104 holds, hawkish-Fed/Dec-hike pressure returns — the force behind STI’s −4.4% week.
  • Silver line: 1,777 oz x $60.42 x 1.2810 ≈ S$137.5k vs S$56.24k loan → equity ≈ S$81.3k ≈ 1.69x; −4% silver day ≈ −6.8% equity.
  • FX ~35% non-SGD; USDSGD 1.2810 steady. Concentration: SG bank/property derating still the week’s net-negative driver.

Alpha (signals, not advice)

  • Xiaomi/HK momentum: +9.72% on SkyNomad 70k pre-orders + short-cover; holding ~25 validates the EV re-rating — counterweight: Sep China autos −24% Y/Y. Tencent ≈425 back at trigger with top southbound volume.
  • SG income pullback maturing: STI −4.4% wk, DBS ~5–6% off highs entering the 5–8% pullback zone; MAS + Q3 GDP this week; STI stabilization above ~5,400 post-MAS = deployment checkpoint for the 10% SGD-income target.
  • Real assets scale-in live: silver bounced +2% off the $59–60 zone, GDX +2.95%; diesel deal gives energy-security premia policy reinforcement. 20% target scale-in live above $60; duration sleeve gated until 10y trades sub-5.20% (Fri 5.24%).

trumpWatch.title: Trump-Putin diesel deal: US waives Russian energy sanctions through April
trumpWatch.detail: Russia to supply 4M+ tonnes of diesel to US/global markets (300k Oct, 500k Nov); US waiving sanctions on Russian energy exports through next April; Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban. Zelensky’s team cut short its US trip after being blindsided; Trump demanded Ukraine halt refinery strikes, said it needs a new president, and threatened to cut intel-sharing/arms. Senators demanded reversal; Tillis warned the deal may be illegal. Trump claimed a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire — Russia has not accepted any ceasefire (Axios). UK pledged to maintain its toughest sanctions regime.

trumpWatch.title: Gulf escalation: 12 killed at Riyadh airport; third tanker mined in Hormuz
trumpWatch.detail: Saudi Arabia said 12 people were killed and 300+ injured in Saturday’s Houthi attack on King Khalid airport; Dammam airport attacked Sunday; Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan-Egypt joint condemnation. Trump is considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis. A third tanker since Saturday struck a naval mine in Hormuz; the US disabled a cargo vessel breaching the blockade in the Gulf of Oman; IRGC warned ships disabling AIS will be treated as hostile. Iran’s SNSC Rezai warned renewed war would hit undersea cables, data centres and AI facilities worth over $2tn. US accepted some of Tehran’s 7 conditions via Qatar; Iran deems it insufficient. Thursday: US sanctioned 17 Iran shadow-fleet vessels.

trumpWatch.title: EU-China reach 16-point consensus; EU caps Chinese hybrid imports
trumpWatch.detail: EU-China talks concluded late Friday with a 16-point consensus covering trade and investment, export controls and IP. The EU announced a cap of 350k Chinese hybrid vehicles in year one, increasing 6% annually, for four years. Last week’s rare-earth retaliation threat has moved into a negotiated track.

trumpWatch.title: AI complex: OpenAI sees $70bn by year-end; NVDA-Reflection, AMZN-Decart talks
trumpWatch.detail: Bloomberg: OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70bn annualized revenue by year-end, repairing Thursday’s FT scare. NVIDIA in talks to raise investment in or acquire Reflection AI (FT). Amazon in discussions to acquire AI startup Decart for about $7bn (WSJ). Trump administration pushing legal liability for AI safety. Firmus shelved its $5bn IPO citing volatility.

trumpWatch.title: Energy plumbing: SPR emergency exchange; IEA urges faster diesel releases
trumpWatch.detail: US authorised an emergency exchange of up to 4M bbl from the SPR for Hurricane Isaias disruptions (4 killed on the Gulf Coast). IEA urged members to accelerate pledged diesel releases and consider additional volumes. Trump told refiners and retailers to begin dropping prices. BP restarting Na Kika and Thunder Horse. Oil executives withdrew from the Riyadh energy congress after the airport missile strikes. Brent settled $104.72 Friday.

trumpWatch.title: China macro: Sep auto sales −24% Y/Y; NDRC vows countercyclical support
trumpWatch.detail: China September passenger-vehicle sales fell 24% Y/Y to 1.7M units; NEV sales declined 12% Y/Y to 1.1M. The NDRC vowed to step up countercyclical support and prepare additional high-impact policy tools; FT cites studies that the debt burden constrains sweeping stimulus. China will launch an AI-skills employment initiative. Singapore Q3 GDP and the MAS October policy statement land this week; Japan and Canada closed Monday.
